    GUI guide

    This guide covers the MultiSolid desktop application: creating cases, running simulations, comparing results, and managing parameter studies. Installation and development setup are in the repository README. For scientific definitions, see the model equations and plugin guide.

    A project contains cases, studies, reusable definitions, and plugins. A case contains its inputs and one latest run. Editing scientific inputs keeps its existing results and marks them stale. Starting another run replaces that case's previous results, including when the new run later fails or is cancelled.

    Task Go to

    Projects and navigation

    The welcome screen offers Create new project, Open existing project, Import archived project, and recent projects. Opening a project resumes it in place. Creating or importing requires a new folder; an existing folder is never merged or overwritten.

    On Windows, the default parent is %USERPROFILE%\Documents\MultiSolid, independent of a Documents location redirected by OneDrive. On other systems it uses the OS Documents location, falling back to ~/Documents/MultiSolid. Browse… selects another parent, and the application remembers a custom creation location. Use a local, writable folder outside the application installation. Project archives can be transferred to synced storage when you want to share inputs.

    The Project menu provides creation, opening, saving, closing, folder access, archives, recent projects, and reusable definitions. Plugins opens the project's scientific definitions. The Help menu opens bundled HTML in your browser, including Getting started, the User guide, reference guides, and Troubleshooting. Help for this screen (F1) opens a dedicated short page for the welcome screen, project screen, each case tab, Project Results, or parameter studies. Search help… opens the help home with search across the bundled pages. Help works offline, including the equations; links marked online require an internet connection.

    About MultiSolid shows application and component versions and lets you preview and copy diagnostic information. Licences and notices shows the application's notices.

    Each case row shows input readiness and the latest run status separately:

    Input status Meaning
    Ready Inputs and the required runtime pass the execution checks.
    Underdefined Some required values are unfinished.
    Invalid Inputs conflict or contain unsupported values.
    Runtime unavailable The selected backend or solver is missing a required component.
    Needs update The case belongs to a study that must be rebuilt.

    Not run, Queued, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled, and Interrupted describe the latest execution. A stale suffix means that run does not match the current scientific inputs or selected plugin contents. It can still be inspected when its files are available.

    Use the row's Run, Duplicate, Edit, and Delete icons. Double-click to edit; press F2 on a case name to rename it. Deleting asks before removing the case and its latest results. Study groups can be collapsed in the case list.

    Recent projects also appear under Project → Recent projects, with their locations and last-interaction times. Opening, editing, and starting execution update recency; background result writes do not. Unavailable folders are omitted. If you move or copy a project, open it once with Open existing project to add its new location. Opening a project elsewhere does not change the preferred parent for newly created projects.

    Create and edit a case

    Choose New Case and give it a name. It starts as an incomplete draft, so select the chemistry and supply the physical inputs before running it. Drafts save automatically, including unfinished values.

    New cases start in Feed mode with Repeat program enabled, 20 axial cells, WENO3 mass and heat schemes, and Compiled / Band execution with one thread and relative tolerance 1e-7. Outlet composition and Outlet conditions plots and their required reports are selected. These defaults do not fill in the bed, species, feed, or a useful time horizon for you.

    The editor has five tabs:

    Tab What you define
    General Simulation duration, reporting interval, spatial discretization, solver, and recorded quantities/plots
    Chemistry Gas and solid species, reaction families, selected reactions, and role bindings
    Bed Geometry, heat transfer, material zones, voidages, and solid loadings
    Program Initial inlet conditions, outlet pressure, and timed hold/ramp steps
    Report An Excel workbook layout using recorded data

    For a new case, it is often easiest to complete Chemistry → Bed → Program, then review General. Red field borders and fills identify missing or invalid values; hover for an explanation. A red tab marker points to a tab with errors. Rules involving several values, such as composition totals, highlight the group. Details… explains errors that cannot be attached to a single field.

    General: numerics and recorded outputs

    Set the simulation horizon, reporting interval, number of cells, and mass/heat schemes. The reporting interval controls saved samples; it is separate from the solver's internal time steps. For a non-repeating program, the horizon is derived from the timed steps and cannot be edited here.

    Choose Backend, Linear solver, Number of threads, and Relative tolerance. Advanced solver settings… exposes additional tolerances and integration controls. See Run simulations for availability and compiled execution.

    Requested reports selects the quantities to record. Requested plots selects plots and identifies the reports they require. Request the quantities you will need before running: changing an Excel layout later cannot create data that were never recorded. The Report tab arranges those data into worksheets; it does not control what the solver records.

    Chemistry: species and reactions

    1. Add gas and solid species from their respective pickers. Each definition shows its source.
    2. Choose + Add reaction families… and add the required models.
    3. Select the reactions to include. Use a family's + Species action to add missing required components.
    4. Inspect Bindings… when a role could refer to more than one selected component, such as two property variants of the same chemical.
    5. Set the new species' gas fractions in Program and solid loadings in Bed as needed. Added values default to 0; removal deletes the species' entries from compositions and zones.

    Selecting a family makes its reactions available; inspect the reaction checkboxes to choose what will run. Rates from overlapping selected models add. If you intend one model to replace another, remove the unwanted selection.

    The reaction graph updates in the background. Click a node to highlight its direct neighbours and connecting links; click again or click empty space to clear the highlight. Scroll or use + / − to zoom, drag to pan, and choose Fit to show the whole graph. The layout refits when the pane resizes.

    The graph uses Graphviz neato. Source installations can use it on PATH or set MULTISOLID_GRAPHVIZ to its executable. See the source installation instructions if it is missing. The packaged desktop application includes Graphviz.

    Bed: geometry and material zones

    Set the radius and length, ambient temperature, heat-transfer coefficient, gas-occupied bed fraction, and flow reversibility. Heat dispersion (W/m/K) sets effective axial heat spreading; 0 disables it. The implemented boundary conditions and transport equations explain these choices.

    Each material-zone row contains its start/end positions, interparticle and intraparticle voidages, particle diameter, and each selected solid's loading. Choose the Solid density basis (bed or solid volume) and Concentration units (mol/m³ or kg/m³) that match your data. Changing these selectors changes how the entered values are interpreted; it does not convert those numbers. The displayed wt% is calculated from the zone's initial loadings and selected molecular weights, not an additional input.

    The first zone starts at zero and the last ends at the bed length. + Add zone splits the final zone, defaults its solid loadings to 0, and leaves its voidages and particle diameter blank. Complete the zones so they cover the bed without gaps or overlaps. Changing a multi-zone bed's length offers fixed or proportionally scaled internal boundaries.

    The preview below the settings displays the sampled bed profiles used by the engine. Use it to inspect your zones after changing boundaries or cell count.

    Program: operating conditions over time

    Set the initial conditions first, then add timed steps.

    Mode How you specify the inlet
    Feed One feed state combines flow, temperature, and composition. A ramp can change selected parts together. Unticked values carry over from the preceding feed.
    Independent channels Flow, temperature, and composition have separate step lists.

    Outlet pressure has its own channel in both modes. Choose Hold to retain the current state for a duration, or Ramp to reach a target over that duration. Targets display their units. Switching modes preserves each mode's inlet steps; the first visit to another mode copies the initial feed values and starts with no inlet steps. Outlet pressure is shared.

    In a composition dialog, new species values default to 0. Set non-negative mole fractions for the gases present so the total is one. Normalize scales a positive total to one while preserving ratios. It becomes available once all entries are valid and their total is positive.

    Repeat program repeats each channel's step list, with an editable overall horizon in General. Each cycle carries forward the previous cycle's final values; add a ramp back to the starting state if the cycle should return there. For a non-repeating program, the longest channel sets the horizon, and every non-empty channel must have the same duration. A non-repeating program with no timed steps needs at least a hold or ramp to define its horizon. Hand-authored CLI inputs can instead specify an explicit horizon with all channels constant.

    Flow basis switches between mol/s and GHSV (h⁻¹). This conversion uses the bed geometry and reference conditions of 273.15 K and 100,000 Pa. Set a positive radius and length before converting existing numeric flows.

    The preview shows the engine's smoothed schedules, repetition, and GHSV conversion. Feed transitions interpolate molar flow, species molar flows, and flow × temperature; see Operating programs. Use a channel's arrow to collapse it, or Focus to give it more room; Show all restores the channels. Preview toolbars support zoom, pan, and image saving.

    First run

    Once you have completed the case inputs in the tabs above:

    1. Choose ← Back to project and check that the case shows Ready. If it does not, open the case and inspect the highlighted inputs or Details….
    2. Choose the case's Run icon. Hover over the icons for their labels.
    3. After Succeeded, open the case, go to General, and choose Show beside an available requested plot. Use Report to prepare an Excel export.

    Checkpoint: the case list shows a successful run and the case can display its retained results. Use Open latest run log if execution fails.

    To compare a changed case with this result, duplicate the original and edit the copy. The original keeps its result; the duplicate starts with copied inputs and report layout but no results.

    If you prefer to start with existing case files, choose Import Case and select their run.yaml. Keep its referenced YAML files alongside it in their original layout. The application copies the inputs into your project and leaves the originals unchanged. Review the imported case's tabs before running it.

    For users who have the source repository, the default case (online) is a complete example. It uses Standard / SuperLU, which importing preserves.

    Run simulations

    Return to the project case list and use a case's Run icon. For a batch, check the cases to include and choose Run all included cases. All included cases are validated before any execution begins; uncheck unfinished drafts. A failure in one running case does not stop the remaining cases.

    Maximum workers controls simultaneous cases and is saved with the project. Each case keeps its own thread setting. The two controls are independent: raising the worker limit does not edit a case's numerical settings. Elapsed time updates while a case is active and freezes when it finishes. Cancel execution stops active workers and their children and cancels the queue.

    Choose a backend and solver

    Backend Offered linear solvers What to expect
    Standard SuperLU, KLU, LAPACK (dense), AztecOO with ILUT / Ifpack ILU / ML, SUNDIALS GMRES with Ifpack ILU Uses the installed DAETools solver adapters.
    Compiled SuperLU, KLU, Band Builds a native model and reuses compatible compiled models. Availability depends on the installed runtime and compiler.

    The dropdown explains unavailable choices. Switching to an incompatible backend or solver asks before updating affected settings; Cancel keeps the original inputs. Imported advanced settings are preserved. An unsupported selection blocks execution instead of silently substituting another solver.

    Both backends need DAETools; Compiled uses it for model construction and initial conditions. Source installations need the matching adapters and native runtime described in the installation guide. The Windows distributions include their compiler, Graphviz, and solver libraries. KLU factorization is serial on both backends.

    Compiled progress and caching

    A first compiled run may spend several minutes generating and compiling its model. Progress distinguishes cache checks, waiting for compilation, generation, and compilation from actual integration. Later compatible cases reuse project/.packed_bed_cache/, including cases in studies. Different operating schedules can share a compiled model while keeping their own program data.

    The cache survives reruns and is excluded from project archives. It can be deleted while the project is idle and will be rebuilt when needed. The project must be writable. For source builds, see the compiled runtime guide.

    What a rerun replaces

    Once a case starts, the new attempt replaces its previous input snapshot, logs, status, and outputs. A later failure or cancellation does not restore the old run. A failed preflight, or cancellation while a case is still queued, leaves its previous results intact.

    Duplicate a case before editing or running a comparison if you want the original result to remain available. Duplicates copy inputs and the Report definition, then start with Not run. Prepared runs use fixed input and plugin copies, so later edits cannot change the inputs associated with a retained result.

    Inspect results

    Open the case and use General → Requested plots → Show for a separate plot window. Available retained NetCDF data can be plotted even when stale. Plot toolbars provide pan, zoom, and image saving.

    Open case folder opens the case's files; its run/ folder contains the latest snapshot, solver log, and outputs. Open latest run log opens worker.log. Outputs include NetCDF data, the engine provenance manifest, and any generated plots.

    Choose Report for one case's Excel workbook, or Results… in the project case list to compare successful runs. A stale result still describes its retained run's inputs, not your current draft. Reports include those retained inputs and provenance.

    Export a case to Excel

    Report opens on the first user worksheet, starting with a blank sheet for a new configuration. Name it and choose what its rows represent (time by default, or any available coordinate axis). Add columns… selects a quantity and values for its other axes. Three species at three positions create nine columns; remove, reorder, or rename individual columns after adding them. Every column heading includes the value unit. Hover over a preview heading to read its full definition.

    Coordinates and available quantities always follow the current case inputs. Row selections support All, First, Last, and Selected values. All columns regenerate when the grid changes; surviving columns keep their labels and order, and manually removed positions stay excluded. First/Last follows the endpoint. Manually selected coordinates that no longer exist are removed with a notice; unfinished inputs preserve selections until coordinates can be calculated again. Missing quantities remain visible for repair. When results exist, the preview shows recorded values and coordinates from the retained run, limited to 20 rows and 12 columns; export contains the full selection. Case information also shows the retained run's inputs and provenance. Before a run, the preview shows expected coordinates and headers and explains why value cells are empty. Editing controls continue to follow current inputs, including when retained results are stale.

    Older saved reports stored every generated coordinate as an exact selection. Re-add those columns with All to enable automatic grid updates; the old format does not record whether they were originally selected individually or with All.

    Export workbook… writes native Excel Tables, with the header row and first column frozen. The fixed first sheet, Case information, contains the retained run's settings, provenance, and an exact dictionary of the exported columns. Stale or partial results can be exported when the selected data and their input snapshot are available. No data are interpolated or silently dropped. Export can be cancelled and only replaces an existing workbook after success.

    Reports autosave with the project independently of scientific inputs. Editing a report does not make results stale, and reports remain editable on generated study cases. Duplicating a case copies its report definition without results. Save as template… writes a portable JSON layout. Apply template… previews its sheets, sizes, and any compatibility issues before replacing the current configuration. Each applied template is an independent editable copy. Templates contain no results, case identity, or run provenance.

    Compare cases in Project Results

    Click Results… beside Run all included cases. A dialog first asks which cases to make available in Results. Only cases whose latest run succeeded and whose result files are present can be selected. Select cases individually or check a study group; filtering also matches factor selections. Select all and Clear all affect every eligible case, including cases hidden by the filter. These checkboxes are independent of Run all inclusion. Cancel keeps the project case list open. Select cases… inside Results reopens the same dialog.

    The worksheet controls work like the case Report tab, with Case as another axis. Choose what rows represent, then Add columns…:

    • Time rows with five cases and three outlet species give 15 value columns.
    • Position rows compare profiles at explicitly selected recorded times.
    • Case rows compare individual recorded values. Time defaults to Last; First/Last resolves separately for each case. This does not calculate an average.

    Shared rows must have the same recorded coordinates. For different grids, use Split by case to replace the current sheet with a separate, editable worksheet for each case, or select row coordinates recorded in all referenced cases. The export never interpolates or silently matches nearby samples. Cell positions and face positions remain separate axes.

    All expands to explicit columns when added, using each case's own grid. Saved columns keep their case identities and coordinate selections. Missing cases or coordinates remain visible for repair after a rerun or study rebuild. First/Last follows the retained run's endpoints; add columns again to include new cases or coordinates. Refresh results reloads the current retained data.

    Preview shows up to 20 rows and 12 columns; Export workbook… exports the full selection as native Excel Tables. The fixed Results information sheet includes run identities, study selections, retained inputs, status, staleness, available balance diagnostics and exact per-case coordinates for every value column. Successful but stale results can be exported if their selected data and snapshot are readable. Missing quantities or samples block the affected worksheet with a reason.

    Save as template… saves the worksheet layout as JSON, without run data or case identities. Apply template… previews the sheets, sizes, compatibility and case mapping before replacing the layout. Select the same number of cases as the template; its case positions map to the selected cases in their displayed order. Applied templates are independent copies, and edits do not change the template file.

    For a failed run, open the individual case's Report tab to export any saved partial data. A normal solver failure can retain samples recorded before the failure. These show the state at reporting times, not rejected solver iterations or necessarily the exact failure instant. A hard crash, forced stop, or failure before recording may leave no exportable data; consult Open latest run log too.

    Use Excel for your own averages, integrals and plots. Project Results layouts autosave and support draft recovery independently of case Report definitions and scientific inputs. Export can be cancelled; an existing workbook is replaced only after success. Existing individual-case plot windows remain available.

    Parameter studies

    Run the intended baseline case successfully first. New Parameter Study accepts only a case whose latest run succeeded, whose current inputs are ready, and whose successful snapshot still matches those inputs. The study copies those inputs as a fixed baseline, records the successful attempt, and does not copy results. Inspect baseline is read-only; Replace baseline selects another successful case. Subsequent changes to the source case do not change the saved baseline. Selected plugins still use the project's current contents for future runs; see Project plugins. The baseline also retains a copy of its report configuration. Every generation or rebuild copies that layout independently into each fresh case, with All axes resolved against that case's inputs. Older studies without a saved report layout capture their source report on their next rebuild, if the source is still available. Study rows have edit and delete icons. Deleting a study asks for confirmation, then removes its generated cases and results while keeping independent cases and reusable definitions.

    The study workspace contains variations beside a live case preview:

    • + Add variation selects a named parameter with units, or a reusable program or bed configuration. Numerical variations accept value lists or linearly spaced ranges. Program fields include initial values, selected step durations, and ramp targets. Step references survive earlier-step deletion and never move silently to another step.
    • All combinations produces the Cartesian product. Explicit case rows specifies individual pairings, with definition dropdowns and numeric cells. The row table supports spreadsheet copy/paste, duplicate, move, remove, and undo/redo. Blank cells remain unfinished.
    • Length sweeps scale all solid-zone boundaries proportionally. Program and bed replacements cannot overlap numerical variations inside the replaced inputs. Timing, species, compositions, geometry, and solver choices use engine validation.
    • Inspect a preview row for the same program and bed plots available in the case editor. Invalid scientific inputs can become draft cases; ambiguous or unfinished variation rules must be repaired before generation. Previews are cancellable.
    • Create N cases writes cases without running them. Generated inputs are read-only; use Edit study or Duplicate as independent case.

    For example, three programs × three bed configurations produce nine cases. With independent Benchmark and Exploratory cases, the project has 11 cases. Benchmark must have succeeded before it is selected as the study baseline. Definitions and the copied baseline do not add simulations to the count.

    Rebuilding a study

    Autosave stores the study rule without changing its generated cases. Changing the baseline, variations, or a referenced definition marks the study Needs rebuild and all its generated cases Needs update. Those cases cannot run until rebuilt; existing results remain inspectable. Reverting the changes clears this requirement. Renaming a study or definition does not require a rebuild.

    Replace X cases with Y deletes every previous generated case in that study, including its inputs, snapshots, logs, and results, then creates fresh cases with new identities, generated names, and default inclusion. Even unchanged combinations are replaced. The preview states the case and result counts before this action. There are no archived cases or restoration. Rebuilds preserve independent cases, other studies, the fixed baseline, and the reusable-definition library.

    Reusable programs and beds

    Use Project → Reusable definitions…, or create/edit definitions while choosing a study variation. Programs contain the operating program, its mode and repetition setting. Bed configurations contain length, radius, ambient temperature, heat-transfer coefficient (U), axial heat dispersion, gas voidage mode, flow reversibility, and solids. The existing input controls edit these definitions with explicit Save / Cancel. Inherited inputs provide preview context. Unused definitions remain in the library; deleting a referenced definition is blocked until its study references are removed.

    Older bed definitions continue inheriting any settings they do not yet contain. Editing and saving them captures these settings from the displayed inputs. A bed variation cannot be combined with a numerical sweep of a setting that bed owns.

    Create desktop studies with New Parameter Study using a successful baseline case. Run all included cases executes included independent and generated cases together, using the project's Maximum workers setting and each case's thread count.

    CLI batches and older studies

    Engine batch.yaml files are used through the CLI (python -m packed_bed batch --help), and cannot be imported as desktop studies. The desktop still supports importing an individual case's run.yaml and importing complete project archives.

    Studies imported by earlier versions remain readable and retain their saved rules. For those existing advanced studies, only settings overridden by the original batch preset apply; other settings still come from the baseline. A pending imported study can still use Add baseline as independent case and Replace baseline to establish a successful baseline. No saved cases or results are removed by retiring the batch-import action.

    Share project inputs

    Choose Project → Export project… to save a .msproject archive. This includes every case (including unfinished drafts), reusable definitions, parameter studies, Report/Results layouts and registered plugins. Results, run snapshots, logs and local settings are excluded. Save the archive outside the project folder; a cancelled or failed export leaves an existing archive unchanged.

    Choose Project → Import project archive…, available even before opening a project. Select the archive, then choose a project name and parent location using the normal creation form. The destination must be a new folder. A successful import opens the project and adds it to Recent projects. Imported cases start at Not run; their saved report layouts can be used again after running the cases. Established study baselines and studies awaiting rebuild retain their state.

    Archives carry the current plugin catalogue, including unused/disabled plugins. Importing and browsing never execute supplied Python code or grant local approval. Use Plugins → Allow code… / Enable when needed. Missing/incompatible packages, damaged archives and unsafe file paths block import with an explanation. Transfers run in a cancellable dialog while the project is idle.

    Project plugins

    Open Plugins beside Project. Register a .msplugin archive or a plugin folder's manifest.yaml, enable it, and select its species or families in Chemistry. Registration alone does not change case selections.

    Plugins in an imported project archive are already registered. Enabled data-only plugins work immediately. For a Python plugin marked Needs local approval, choose Allow code… and wait for Checks passed. Disabled plugins remain disabled until enabled.

    Importing and browsing do not execute plugin Python. Approval permits code to run with your user permissions during checks and simulations; workers are not a security sandbox. Approval stays on this computer. Code/resource changes require approval again; manifest parameter edits do not.

    Cases and studies use the current contents of their selected project plugins for future runs, including studies with a fixed baseline. Retained run snapshots keep their original plugin copies. The plugin guide explains variants, replacement, updates, and sharing; the example walkthrough teaches plugin creation.

    Saving and recovery

    Case inputs, Report definitions, Project Results layouts, and study rules save after a short pause, including unfinished values. Project → Save Project, switching projects, and closing flush pending edits, including the active table cell. If saving fails, the draft stays in the editor and navigation is blocked; read the reason in the status bar and resolve the write problem before leaving.

    Edits create a recovery checkpoint in .drafts/ before the autosave delay. After an interruption, opening the project offers:

    Choice Effect
    Recover drafts Restore the unfinished edits and reassess readiness and staleness.
    Discard drafts Keep the saved inputs and discard the recovery edits.
    Cancel Leave the recovery decision pending without opening the project.

    Recovery preserves retained run snapshots and results. It does not resume a solver. Unfinished retained runs are marked Interrupted after reopening. Project and execution locks prevent concurrent access.

    An input archive excludes run data. To retain a full project with its latest results, close it and copy the entire project folder. Each case still has only one latest run; the copied folder does not provide a history of earlier attempts.

    Troubleshooting

    Problem What to check
    Run is unavailable Check input readiness, highlighted tabs, and Details…. Complete the draft or resolve its runtime requirement.
    Run all refuses to start Every included case must pass validation. Uncheck unfinished cases or rebuild cases marked Needs update.
    First compiled run seems slow Check whether progress says generating or compiling. The first build can take several minutes; later compatible runs use the cache.
    Solver is unavailable Read the dropdown's explanation. For a source installation, check DAETools adapters, compiler, and native runtime setup.
    Chemistry graph is missing Check Graphviz neato or MULTISOLID_GRAPHVIZ, then use Retry in the graph pane.
    A composition will not normalize Enter every species value, keep them non-negative, and ensure the total is positive.
    Program horizon cannot be edited Non-repeating programs derive it from timed steps. Match all non-empty channel durations or enable repetition and set the horizon.
    A new species makes the case incomplete Gas fractions and solid-zone loadings default to 0. Check that gas fractions sum to one and inspect reaction bindings.
    A plugin has no effect Select its definitions in Chemistry or use the plugin replacement action. See the plugin guide.
    Results are stale Inputs or selected plugin contents have changed. Inspect/export the retained run, or run the case again for current inputs.
    A plot or workbook lacks a quantity Check whether that quantity was recorded in the retained run. Request it in General and rerun if needed.
    Cases cannot share a Results worksheet Select exactly shared recorded row coordinates or use Split by case. Export does not interpolate.
    A failed run is missing from Project Results Use that case's Report tab for any saved partial samples and inspect its log. Project Results selects successful runs.
    A study baseline cannot be selected Run a ready case successfully and keep its inputs unchanged before selecting it.
    A study case cannot be edited Edit the study or duplicate the generated case as an independent case. Report layouts remain editable.
    Saving or opening is blocked Read the status message, check write access, and close another process using the project. Preserve the open draft until saving succeeds.
    A moved project is missing from Recent projects Open its new location with Open existing project.

    Appendix: project files and developer reference

    project/
  project.json                   # name, cases, studies, max_workers, registered plugins
  plugins/<plugin-id>/current/    # current registered plugin files
  .drafts/                       # recovery checkpoints for unfinished edits
  .packed_bed_cache/             # reusable compiled models; excluded from archives
  cases/<case-id>/
    inputs/                      # run/program/solids/chemistry.yaml for this case
    run/                         # one latest execution, replaced on rerun
      inputs/                    # fixed inputs associated with the latest result
      snapshot.json              # input hashes, fingerprint, case/attempt identity
      status.json
      worker.log
      output/                    # NetCDF, engine manifest, and plots
  studies/<study-id>/
    study.json                   # rule, fixed-baseline provenance, stable step targets
    baseline/                    # four copied scientific documents
    batch.yaml                   # compatibility: rule saved by an older batch import
  definitions/<definition-id>/   # metadata plus program.yaml or solids.yaml
  execution.json                 # latest Run case / Run all queue status
  execution.log                  # worker startup diagnostics

    Prepared snapshots briefly live in .pending-<attempt> beside a case's run/. Once validated, a snapshot replaces that case's run folder; .previous-run is a short-lived backup during the directory swap. Recovery completes an interrupted swap. Attempt identities distinguish worker events; they are not run history. Input/metadata files use atomic replacement. Study and definition writes use a staged directory transaction. Rebuilding commits project metadata only after staging the complete replacement case set. Before that commit, recovery restores old cases; after it, recovery deletes temporary backups. Recovery runs before loading case inputs. Project archives transfer saved definitions and exclude recovery checkpoints and run data.

    File publication and temporary-directory cleanup share the engine's file_io.py (online) policy. Status files, results, manifests, cache records, plugin files and exports use unique temporary files before atomic replacement. Brief Windows reader locks are retried for up to 0.75 seconds; permanent access errors still surface. Run/study folder swaps use the same retry policy while retaining their existing rollback order. Export cancellation is checked again before each replacement attempt. Temporary-file and scratch-directory cleanup preserve the original failure if cleanup also fails.

    The application reads the current project format (3) and run-snapshot format (1). Older project formats are rejected rather than migrated. Project and solver locks prevent concurrent access. Reopening after an interrupted session marks unfinished retained runs as Interrupted.

    File Responsibility
    window.py (online) Welcome screen, project case list, navigation, and actions
    case_list.py (online) Collapsible study groups, case status, inclusion, and icon actions
    editor.py (online) Shared input controls, read-only inspection, case autosave, and retained plots
    studies.py (online) Parameter catalogue, pure expansion, validation, and generation signatures
    study_store.py (online) Baseline eligibility, persistence/imports, and transactional complete rebuilds
    study_editor.py (online) Study workspace, variation dialogs, and cancellable previews
    study_tables.py (online) Preview and explicit-row models, spreadsheet paste, and definition dropdowns
    definition_editor.py (online) Reusable-definition library and shared inspection dialogs
    inputs.py (online) Explicit draft initialization, input validation, timing, and zone scaling
    general.py (online) Numerical/solver settings and report/plot selections
    chemistry.py (online) Species lists and reaction families
    reaction_graph.py (online) Asynchronous Graphviz SVG preview, node highlighting, zoom and pan
    bed.py (online) Geometry, material zones, and reactor boundary rules
    program_editor.py (online) Program modes, hold/ramp tables, feed targets, timing, and flow conversion
    editor_widgets.py (online) Shared selection lists, tables, and preview canvases
    project.py (online) Project/case storage, imports, readiness, and run preparation
    execution.py (online) Start, monitor, and stop the project's worker with Qt
    worker.py (online) Verify/activate snapshots, collect logs, publish status, call the shared engine loop
    results.py (online) Project Results, using the shared Report worksheet controls
    project_results.py (online) Case-axis selections, native-grid validation and project Excel export
    batch.py (online) Shared case scheduling, concurrency, thread limits, and worker cleanup
    preview.py (online) Scientific preview arrays without Qt or plotting imports

    Study selectors and the project library share DefinitionList and its editing actions. Both the workspace and storage use preview_study(); its lazy mode lets Qt consume one captured preview incrementally. Shared document access, scientific fingerprint inputs, timing, and scaling live in inputs.py.

    ProjectCase.resolve() uses the engine's metadata-only inspect_case(). Workers load the snapshots and call run_case() with its optional status callback. The UI and batch CLI both use run_cases_in_processes() for concurrent scheduling and worker cleanup. The CLI retains its in-process path for one worker with no timeout.

    Each project stores one current copy of each plugin; Save replaces that copy. Code/resource approval belongs to the local computer and survives parameter edits. Workers reconstruct authoritative definitions from plugin copies in their input snapshots. See the plugin guide for workflows and the API.

    Source setup and packaging checks

    Use the repository installation and development instructions. Opening projects and generating numerical previews with built-in definitions do not require DAETools. Python plugins may require it when their implementations load; both execution backends require it. From an activated source environment, packed-bed-ui and python -m packed_bed_ui launch the same application. An optional argument may be a project folder or its project.json.

    For relevant engine or packaging changes, run these from the repository root:

    python -m packed_bed examples/simulations/default_case/run.yaml --validate-only
python -m packed_bed.compiled.smoke
python -m pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation --wheel-dir build/wheels ./desktop

    The compiled smoke check requires a working compiler and a managed native runtime including KLU; the scikit-SUNDAE wheel alone does not supply KLU. Wheel building checks desktop packaging separately. See Building the Windows distribution for release isolation, runtime staging, and installer/portable builds.

    The interface follows system light/dark appearance and uses a shared numeric font. Maratype supplies the wordmark, project title, and M/S ribbon; its font notice (online) stays beside the asset. The launch splash appears before the workspace loads; solver workers run without it.
